story.head: Tired legs for the Avalanche
paras: The Ducks (11-10-1) lost 8-6 to St. Louis on Tuesday, and the Avalanche (12-7-3) lost 4-1 to Utah last night. Going in, the Ducks are third in the Pacific (tied for 17th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 11th).

The Ducks hit a lot (4th), give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). Anaheim has scored 3.86 goals a game, the fourth most in the league, and allowed 3.86, the third most. As for the Avalanche, they get their defensemen shooting (1st) and do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest). Colorado has scored 3.91 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Ducks. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Avalanche (1st), so expect an open game.

Cutter Gauthier (21 G / 8 A / 29 P in 21 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind, with five goals in eight games against Colorado since 2023-24. For the Avalanche, Martin Nečas (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (15 G / 6 A / 21 P in 22 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, fifth in the NHL.

Lukáš Dostál (4-5-1 / .858 SV% in 11 GS) has struggled for Anaheim so far, but is expected to start. Scott Wedgewood (1-3-2 / .863 SV% in 6 GS) has struggled for Colorado so far, but is expected to start. Wedgewood has a .947 save percentage in five starts against the Ducks, well above his usual .904. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Ducks do.
